rationale: Two threads close and one opens. (1) The backlog finding is now complete: receipt 78d56323ae6646da8140c38ebed9bd1c executes the corrected declaration and returns comparison 0 violated (witness event index 9: newraft_returned false after the bounded 15 s wait for 8402 committed entries) and comparison 1 holds (evaluated event index 7: newraft_returned true after 2 ms for 8002 entries), so the blocking is bracketed by its own control. (2) The strongest consequence left unwitnessed under the configuration-loss question is whether authority is ever regained: a node that comes back with no configuration cannot campaign, which turns an inconsistent membership view into a cluster that never recovers leadership. A bounded sampling experiment is submitted for that, with the flag-off case as control. (3) The configuration-loss interpretation itself is unchanged and is not restated.

investigations.question: After that restart, does the node ever regain authority within a bounded window, or does the configuration it failed to rebuild leave it permanently unable to campaign?
investigations.hypothesis: With an empty or snapshot-age configuration, runFollower takes the 'no known peers' branch and the hasVote gate never opens, so the node stays Follower and the single-voter cluster never regains a leader.
investigations.discriminator: Restart the same single-node state with the flag on and off and sample the node's state for a bounded window: the control should reach Leader, the flagged case should stay Follower.

knowledge.statement: With Config.RestoreCommittedLogs enabled and no snapshot, NewRaft replays the committed log by pushing one fsmMutateCh message per MaxAppendEntries-sized batch before the FSM goroutine is started; when the committed backlog requires more batches than the queue's 128 slots, the send blocks and NewRaft never returns, so the node never starts.
knowledge.conditions: Config.RestoreCommittedLogs=true with a CommitTrackingLogStore, no snapshot covering the committed range, and a restored commit index whose replay needs more than 128 batches of MaxAppendEntries entries (default 64, about 8192 entries); observed for 8402 entries (132 batches) with a bounded 15 second wait, against 8002 entries (126 batches) returning in 0-3 ms.

gaps.question: Does the same loss of configuration occur when a snapshot exists whose configuration index is below the index of a committed LogConfiguration entry (entries in (snapshotIndex, restored commitIndex])?

interpretations.rationale: Receipt 78d56323ae6646da8140c38ebed9bd1c (exit 0, ten events, no parse loss) resolves both comparisons of the corrected declaration. Comparison 0 is violated by witness event index 9: with RestoreCommittedLogs on, no snapshot and 8402 committed entries (commit index 8402, admission event index 8), NewRaft had not returned after the bounded 15 second wait. Comparison 1 holds at evaluated event index 7: the same restart with 8002 committed entries returned in 2 ms, so the two sizes bracket the failure and rule out general replay slowness. Source mechanism: NewRaft creates fsmMutateCh with capacity 128 (api.go:558-561) and starts the FSM, main and snapshot goroutines only after the startup work at api.go:632-639, while restoreFromCommittedLogs (api.go:724-754) calls processLogs, which pushes one message per MaxAppendEntries batch into that queue (raft.go:1296-1320); a replay needing more than 128 batches blocks on an unconsumed channel inside NewRaft with no retry, timeout or fallback in that path. Consequence: the node never finishes starting, so duties that depend on it (elections, replication, convergence) are stalled indefinitely rather than bounded; the boundary near 8192 committed entries with default MaxAppendEntries of 64 and default TrailingLogs of 10240 keeps this inside ordinary settings. The earlier receipt 04fccedbacf54df3b7064fd16fa57b26 already witnessed the violation but could not complete the control because both sizes shared one result event name; it is retained as prior evidence of the same behaviour.

knowledge.assertion: NewRaft blocks forever on an unconsumed fsmMutateCh when the RestoreCommittedLogs replay needs more batches than the queue holds.

counterevidence: The sub-capacity case returns immediately in two independent receipts (0 ms and 2 ms for 8002 entries), so the outcome is not general slowness.
No snapshot existed in either case, so the blocking is independent of snapshot restore.
limitations: The failing case is a bounded wait, not an infinite-run proof; a later repair or a different schedule is not excluded by this observation alone.
The queue capacity of 128 and the batch size of 64 are read from the source, not measured.
The failure was observed with the in-memory commit-tracking store; whether a durable store changes the size boundary is not established.

interpretations.rationale: Source: the restarted node's configuration is empty in the no-snapshot case (api.go:604-620 with restoreFromCommittedLogs at api.go:724-754), and runFollower only campaigns when hasVote holds while an empty latest configuration takes the 'no known peers, aborting election' branch (raft.go:228-246); quorumSize() would also be computed from that empty configuration (raft.go:1087-1094). A native construction probe of a single-voter cluster restarted after ten applied entries measured the predicted difference: with the flag on the node stayed Follower and became_leader was false over a 1500 ms window (ElectionTimeout is 50 ms), while the flag-off control reached Leader with after_latest_index 1. That probe is construction feedback without a retained receipt, so the submitted experiment re-runs both cases under controller execution; only its receipt can make this comparison complete.
counterevidence: The control restart reaches Leader in the same window, so the non-campaigning is not a general restart delay.
limitations: No receipt yet; the account rests on source reading plus a native probe.
Only a single-voter configuration is exercised, so election outcomes under a stale multi-voter membership are not witnessed here.
The window is bounded, so a much later recovery is not excluded.

scope.description: Boot a single-voter cluster with CommitTrackingLogs, commit ten entries, shut down, restart from the same stores, then sample the node's raft state every 10 ms for a bounded 1500 ms window (ElectionTimeout is 50 ms) and report whether leadership was ever acquired. Run with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs true and false.
assumptions: A single-voter configuration normally regains leadership within a few election timeouts, which the 1500 ms window covers by a wide margin.
No snapshot exists, so the snapshot path cannot supply the configuration.
Sampling does not perturb the node; the state is read through the library's own accessor.
excluded: Multi-voter election outcomes, which the single-voter scenario cannot witness.
The startup-blocking finding, which is a separate question.

experiment.prefix: The harness boots one node with CommitTrackingLogs and RestoreCommittedLogs, applies ten commands, records the committed configuration index, shuts down, and restarts with NewRaft on the same logs, stable and snapshots stores plus a fresh inmem transport. It then polls getState() for a bounded window and emits authority_after_restart with became_leader, the final state name, the sample window and the configuration index observed after the restart; a startup_before_restart event carries the same mode identity and the pre-restart state, and no production logic is modified.
experiment.responsibility: The library owns the state a node resumes with: once a committed configuration exists in its log, a restart must not leave it permanently unable to participate, which the caller cannot repair through the public API.

comparisons.description: A single-voter cluster restarted from its own committed state is expected to regain leadership inside the bounded window; the defect prediction is that it never campaigns.
Control: the identical restart without the flag is expected to reach Leader, separating the lost configuration from any general restart delay.
